title: SDK & API Launch: Release Notes Staging, Back-compat Strategy, and Sample Snippet Library
creator: Ava Chen
description: Coordinate generation, staging, and approval of release notes and a portable code snippet library for the SDK and API surface (function calling, structured output, streaming). Produce localized release notes, a curated snippet gallery for Go/Python/TS, and a staging plan to validate backward-compatibility claims before GA.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical release notes drafted and staged in the release-notes repo with clear breaking/migration guidance
Snippet library contains runnable examples for Go, Python, and TypeScript covering: function calling, structured output, streaming, and error handling
Localization pack (EN, DE, FR, JP) prepared and reviewed by localization team
Legal and security sign-off on any wording implying SLA or data guarantees
Release notes approved in the release channel and linked from SDK README before push to prod
Backward-compatibility smoke tests executed on top-10 customer prompts with no regressions or documented mitigations

decisions: Keep release notes canonical copy in docs repo and generate localized variants from it (avoid multiple source of truth)
Ship snippet gallery as a separate 'examples' package in the SDK monorepo so we can iterate without bumping core SDK versions
Include a 'breaking_changes' section only when behavior changes affect customer-facing API contracts; otherwise use 'migration_tips'
Run canary rollout for streaming endpoints to 5% of traffic in staging before full rollout to production
risks: Localization delays could push final approvals past scheduled release window
Snippet CI flakiness could block publishing — mitigation: add retries and containerized reproducibility
Undiscovered compatibility regressions for customers pinning old SDK versions
Legal review may require rewording that affects marketing messaging
release_notes_outline: Summary: high-level bullets about features (function calling, structured output, streaming improvements)
Highlights: top 3 developer-facing improvements and expected impact
Migration guide: step-by-step for customers with pinned model versions or custom wrappers
Code snippets: short examples (Go, Python, TS) for typical flows
Changelog: low-level commits and PR references
sample_snippets_index: examples/py/function_calling_simple.py - demonstrates function calling with structured JSON schema
examples/py/streaming_chat.py - streaming responses with reconnect handling
examples/py/structured_output_validation.py - validate structured output against JSON schema
examples/go/function_calling.go - idiomatic Go wrapper with error handling
examples/ts/structured-output.ts - TypeScript example with zod runtime validation
examples/ts/streaming-react-hook.tsx - React hook for streaming token UI
sample_snippets_prs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/482 - add TypeScript streaming example and CI job
https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/487 - add Python examples and test harness
https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/491 - add Go examples and module packaging for examples
rollout_plan: Stage: merge docs PR to staging branch and deploy to staging docs site
Canary: enable new streaming and function-calling flags for 5% of internal staging traffic
Validation: run top-10 customer prompt suite and automated snippet CI
Ramp: 25% traffic for 24h, monitor errors and latency; if stable, move to 100%
Post-rollout: open feedback window for 7 days and fast-fix any regressions
localization_plan: Primary source is canonical EN notes in docs repo
L10n team to produce DE/FR/JP variants and upload to docs/l10n folder
Review cycle: 2 days per locale, with PM and Docs reviewer for each
If L10n misses release window, publish EN first and add localized badges linking to 'translations coming'
qa_plan: Automated snippet CI: compile and run smoke assertions across languages
Backward-compatibility smoke tests: run top-10 customer prompts and diff token-level outputs
Manual exploratory: Docs engineer to walk through tutorial examples on Windows, macOS, Linux
Support validation: Support runbook updated with sample troubleshooting steps
